Subject: Observability hooks - spec and sample headers (attachment)

Hi Jordan / team — attaching a short spec and a tiny headers sample that you can drop into your gateway / sidecar. See the attached files: redwood-observability-specs.pdf and redwood-sdk-sample-headers.txt. Below are the recommended header names and formats (summary):

1) Trace ID (stable; 128-bit hex recommended)
Header: X-Redwood-Trace-Id
Example: X-Redwood-Trace-Id: 4f8b3c2a9d1e4f7ab2c9ef1d6a3b4c5e
Notes: propagate inbound trace id if present; otherwise generate at your edge. We recommend 128-bit hex to avoid collisions.

2) Latency breakdown header
Header: X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown
Example: X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: compile=12;queue=6;exec=132;kv_cache_hit=true
Notes: semicolon-delimited key=value pairs. Keys: compile, queue, exec, kv_cache_hit (boolean). Values in ms. SDK and proxies should parse and forward this header into traces/span attributes.

3) Timing / hop headers (optional)
Header: X-Redwood-Timing
Example: X-Redwood-Timing: edge=5;ingest=3;model_exec=128

4) Logging fields we emit in structured logs (JSON fields recommended):
- redwood_request_id (UUID)
- redwood_trace_id (string matching header)
- model_name (string)
- model_version (string)
- prompt_tokens (int)
- response_tokens (int)
- latency_ms (int)

5) Auth recommendation
- Use short-lived service tokens minted via your internal vault; Redwood supports JWT bearer tokens for service-to-service auth. Header: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- For user-scoped requests (if you need user-level tracking), use a delegated token pattern — we can share a sample flow.

6) SDK propagation snippet (pseudo node):
```
const headers = {
  'Authorization': `Bearer ${SERVICE_TOKEN}`,
  'X-Redwood-Trace-Id': incomingHeaders['x-request-id'] || generateTraceId(),
  'X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown': '' // left empty; Redwood runtime returns populated header
};
await fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', { method: 'POST', headers, body });
```

7) Dashboards / joins
- In your tracing system (Jaeger/Tempo/Lightstep) join on redwood_trace_id and redwood_request_id.
- We recommend creating a latency-breakdown panel that parses X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown and sums exec+queue+compile to compare against measured end-to-end latency.

Attachments: redwood-observability-specs.pdf (one-page spec), redwood-sdk-sample-headers.txt (plain text examples).

Let me know if you want us to open a short RFC issue in your repo for the integration steps; happy to pair.

-Ethan
